terms.gloss: carry out the dung, muck out
evidence: Cato Agr. 39: stercus in stercilīnum ēgeritō
terms.comment: Cato’s phrase for a job to be done in bad weather, with the order to clean the cowshed, the sheepfold, the yard, and the farmhouse (bene pūrgātō). The plain verb for cleaning out a stall is pūrgō (see “clean”).

evidence: Col. 7.6.6: dīligēnsque pāstor cotīdiē stabulum converrit
terms.comment: Of goats’ stalls, swept every day so that no dung or wet is left standing.

phrases.latin: Gallīnārium sordet; stercus in sterquilīnium ēgerāmus.
phrases.english: The hen-house is dirty; let’s muck it out onto the compost heap.

phrases.latin: Ubi tempestātēs malae erunt, cum opus fierī nōn poterit, stercus in stercilīnum ēgeritō. Bubīle, ovīle, cohortem, vīllam bene pūrgātō.
phrases.english: When the weather is bad and no work can be done, carry the dung out to the dung heap. Clean the cowshed, the sheepfold, the yard, and the farmhouse well.

phrases.latin: dīligēnsque pāstor cotīdiē stabulum converrit nec patitur stercus aut ūmōrem cōnsistere
phrases.english: and a careful herdsman sweeps out the stall every day and does not let dung or wet lie

phrases.latin: gallīnāria semper fūmigābimus et ēmundāta stercore līberābimus
phrases.english: we shall always smoke out the hen-houses, and clean them and rid them of droppings

sources: Lewis & Short: egero · Lewis & Short: converro
